input.question: Why kangaroos are found in Australia only?
input.ground_truth: There is a single species of a genus of kangaroo in Papua New Guinea, a country just north of Australia, so kangaroos as a group are not entirely localised to Australia. Their relatives are other marsupial species found in south america (approx 100 species). [Marsupials as a whole are thought to have evolved in South America despite the majority being found in Australia!](_URL_0_). They then spread through ancient gondwana to Australia and established the orders that we still have today (we know this because there are south american marsupials more closely related to Australian marsupials than other south american ones). After the split up, modern marsupials evolved in their unique environments. The ones in antartica died when it got too cold (edit: we have their fossils though, and they also seem south american).
